excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
With the current CL implementation of the builder API, all blocks must be verified by a local EE before they are attested to. This prevents finalization of invalid blocks.

FB's original approach was to be a "middleware", where they become the canonical source of truth for payload validity for CLs. In such a scenario it's trivial for FB to finalize an invalid payload.

We're looking at the choice between (a) allowing FB to finalize whatever they want and (b) having more FB blocks on the network. I don't claim that anything here is "strictly" better or worse with CL integration of the builder API and I would be very cautious about anyone doing so.

excerpts.content: It is basically the same sentiment as we have for people who offload their EL to a third party.  We can't stop you (at the moment), but if it goes bad we won't bail you out no matter how big you are, and we are working on writing code that will make it so we *can* stop you.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: What about "use FB at your own risk, we wont bail you out when the thing collapses" but also with "we'll help you do it right"?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I define "right" here as in "in a non-censorious way".  If FB team isn't willing to stop censoring, then I don't think it is possible to "do it right", given my definition of right.

excerpts.author: izz.y
excerpts.content: define "non-censorious"

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Meaning they aren't censoring transactions from/to certain addresess/nationalities for all users of their relay.

excerpts.author: izz.y
excerpts.content: that sounds like a personal definition which isn't practical or related to how the protocol actually works, though

excerpts.author: izz.y
excerpts.content: a block proposer can basically decide what to put in a block, that's their right as per how the protocol is designed

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It is the entire reason we are building this thing, to put a stop to financial censorship.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: A block *proposer*, yes.  But the relay is a highly centralized entity that we (core Ethereum community) are integrating with.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If individual proposers censor, we can't stop them and while I frown on it and look forward to CR lists when we *can* stop them, I don't think we should be blessing software that is actively censoring on a large scale right out of the gate.

excerpts.author: izz.y
excerpts.content: I don't think that's actually happening, though

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The FB relay has been censoring for over a year already on mainnet.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It is just that previously they only censored a handful of addresses that no one used so it didn't really matter and everyone ignored it.

excerpts.author: izz.y
excerpts.content: their RPC you mean?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: No, the relay itself.
